{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABejM7UQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIERJ8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 327, "title": "Auto-download missing required models when a Live execution window opens", "body": "## Goal

When a Live execution window opens, **automatically download any missing required model assets before initializing the runtime**, instead of failing and forcing the user to navigate to Models or re-save a graph. Keep Start disabled until downloads, verification, and model initialization complete.

This is a **fallback** in addition to existing proactive asset preparation following successful Graph Editor Auto Save. A saved graph must remain runnable even when its required files were never downloaded, were evicted/deleted, or are still being prepared in another tab.

## Existing behavior

- `extension/recorder.js` opens a Live session and calls `session.prepareModels()` immediately.
- `extension/session.js` prepares an inert execution runtime and initializes required model instances before allowing Start. Errors tell the user to save the graph or recover in Models, then press Retry models.
- `docs/extension-graph.md` explicitly states: “Live initialization is cache-only: it cannot recover missing, corrupt or evicted optional weights by downloading.”
- Graph Editor Auto Save already prepares and verifies required model *files* asynchronously, separately from inference-worker initialization.
- `extension/model-asset-cache.js` provides verified downloaded-asset cache management (with locking, cancellation, retries, integrity verification). Do not duplicate model download implementations.

## Required behavior

1. Upon opening Live, resolve the **chosen saved graph** (not an unrelated/default graph), its expanded subgraph dependencies, and the models needed by its **executable** paths. Inspect cache availability/integrity for these requirements.
2. If any required assets are missing/corrupt/evicted, **automatically prepare/download only those missing assets**, reusing the existing verified cache pipeline, pinned manifests, and concurrency controls. Never download every model or unrelated models.
3. Preserve shared disk-cache behavior: identical model files/manifests used by multiple graphs/windows must be downloaded **once**, with other sessions awaiting/reusing the same verified result. Account for simultaneous Live windows, Auto Save preparation, Web dictation, Models manual preparation, and cache eviction/deletion races.
4. Show actionable Live status and download progress, preferably model names and verified/total bytes when available (e.g. “Downloading model…”, then “Preparing models…”). **Start stays disabled** until all required downloads, validation, and inference-worker/GPU initialization succeed; then display **Ready** and enable Start, subject to existing other admission conditions.
5. When assets are already cached and verified, skip the download and retain the current fast Live preparation path. Model-free executable graphs should show Ready without downloading.
6. If a download fails, is offline, canceled, storage quota is exceeded, checksum validation fails, or runtime initialization fails, show a clear reason and a usable **Retry models** action **inside Live**. Retrying must re-check/reuse intact cached files and must not require navigating to Models or Graph Editor.
7. Keep the auto-download confined to an **explicit execution context** (opening a Live window for a particular graph); do not start inference, audio capture, microphone permissions, or playback until existing Start and user-gesture conditions are met. Download preparation must not execute graph nodes or generate output.
8. Preserve session ownership and lifecycle isolation: closing/Stop/canceling a Live window must cancel/tear down that window's work safely without corrupting a shared download required by another consumer. Discard stale progress/completion after switching saved graphs or closing. Opening another window must not tear down an existing session.
9. Keep current treatment of active sessions: saved edits never silently replace a running graph; changes take effect on a subsequent session. Do not reuse an already-active runtime for a different graph.
10. This behavior should work for **all model types**, including ReazonSpeech and Silero VAD once [#323](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/323) migrates those from bundled data to on-demand cached model assets.
11. Respect [#326](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/326): the shared download layer should make its one-time best-effort persistent-storage request on the first actual download. Permission denial must not block preparation.
12. Update Live help/error text and docs to remove the obsolete “Save graph or go to Models first” cache-only restriction. Models remains available for manual management but **not required** for ordinary Live startup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clean cache: opening Live with a saved graph containing a downloadable model automatically starts download, shows progress, prepares the runtime, then enables Start when ready.
- [ ] Fully cached graph: no download, and existing initialization-to-Ready behavior remains.
- [ ] Partial/corrupt/evicted cache: only missing or invalid files are re-downloaded and reverified.
- [ ] Graph with no required model: Ready without network or model downloads.
- [ ] Two Live windows (or Live + Auto Save/Models) requiring the same model share the download and verified cache, not duplicate file transfers.
- [ ] Offline/network failure/storage quota failure/invalid checksum: clear error; Start disabled; Retry models works after conditions improve without leaving Live.
- [ ] Cancel, close, graph replacement, and concurrent sessions do not leak workers, retain stale status, corrupt cache or cancel downloads belonging to others.
- [ ] Ready is emitted only after model *runtime initialization* succeeds, not merely after downloaded files are cached.
- [ ] Web microphone and Live capture/Start permission behavior is unchanged.
- [ ] Relevant integration, browser, and concurrency tests pass.

## Likely implementation touchpoints

- `extension/session.js` (`TabSession.prepareModels`, retry/cancel, model state/progress and runtime readiness)
- `extension/recorder.js` and Live UI/stylesheet for progress and retry/status
- `extension/graph-model-preparation.js`, existing model manifest resolvers and `extension/model-asset-cache.js` for dependency identification, shared verified downloads, and file-only preparation
- `tests/live-model-preparation.test.js` and `tests/extension/live-model-preparation.spec.js`; extend with clean/partial cache, concurrency, failures, retry, cancellation and graph swap
- `docs/extension-graph.md` and user-facing recovery descriptions

## Coordination

- [#323](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/323): unified on-demand cache lifecycle for **all** AI models; avoid implementing a special case for the former bundled ASR/VAD.
- [#326](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/326): automatic persistent-storage request from the shared download layer.
- [#299](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/299): Graph Editor Auto Save and proactive model asset preparation; Live's missing-model fallback supplements it.
- Retain the existing one-session-per-window inference ownership model; **cross-window inference memory sharing is not in scope**.
